title: Chinese ties and low-carbon industrialization in Africa
summary: The paper examines how Chinese greenfield investment in African manufacturing affects industrial carbon emissions. It finds that Chinese FDI inflows increased industrial emissions, especially when they targeted labour- and resource-intensive sectors.
keyFindings: Chinese FDI inflows increased industrial carbon emissions in Africa.
The effect is strongest when Chinese FDI targets labour- and resource-intensive manufacturing.
Host-country environmental regulation moderates the effect, but not significantly, pointing to weak enforcement.
methods: Panel of Chinese greenfield FDI into manufacturing in 34 African countries, 2003–2014, estimated with a Lewbel instrumental variable approach.
